reasons: The cited text supports the compliant classification: §9(b) contains affirmative express warranties covering the rule's material elements — performance to industry standards (p0034), no malicious code (p0036), services free from errors materially affecting utility and conforming to the Agreement (p0038), and ongoing compliance with applicable Laws (p0041).

Duration is at or better than the preferred position: the warranties are not time-boxed and run 'now and throughout the Term,' exceeding the 12-month/90-day benchmark. The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact (no numeric period stated because none is needed), not a substantive gap.

The §13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties — it opens 'Except as expressly set forth herein' and expressly excepts 'the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement,' so the walk-away 'AS IS with all warranties disclaimed' scenario is not present.

Absence of a repair/replace/refund remedy sentence is not a material failure here: there is no sole/exclusive-remedy language, so Customer retains all remedies at law plus the §4(b) cure/termination right. Inserting the model 'at Vendor's option' remedy would narrow our position, and the playbook directs not to flag terms that benefit our party.

Remaining gaps (conformance to 'industry standards' rather than documentation; no separate 'professional and workmanlike' formulation) are minor sub-elements properly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was rendered and no counterparty comment was proposed; the output paragraphs are unchanged from the originals.
